c.tagline: Romantic Germany distilled — a castle ruin, the oldest university, and the Neckar valley.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and regulated; you can hail on the street, wait at a rank, or book by phone or app. Ride-hailing apps FreeNow, Uber and Bolt also operate.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number for ambulance and fire; 110 reaches the police. Both are free and staffed by English-speaking operators.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Petty pickpocketing can occur in the Hauptstrasse tourist crowds and around Bismarckplatz and the main station late at night.

hood_desc: Heidelberg's postcard old town: a long pedestrian spine of Renaissance and baroque houses running from Bismarckplatz to the Karlstor, beneath the red-sandstone castle ruins and beside the Old Bridge over the Neckar. Home to the Marktplatz, the Church of the Holy Spirit and the historic university quarter; best for first-timers who want every sight on foot.

A leafy, affluent residential district across the Neckar reached by the Old Bridge, with elegant villas, the start of the Philosophers' Walk (Philosophenweg) and its river-and-castle views, plus quiet cafes; suits travellers who want calm, greenery and the classic panorama of the old town.

A convenient quarter just west of the old town around the main hospitals and Bergheimer Strasse, within walking distance of both the Altstadt and the train station and lined with mid-range and chain hotels; a practical, well-connected base.

An elegant late-19th-century grid of stucco townhouses, tree-lined streets and squares between the old town and the station — one of Germany's best-preserved Gruenderzeit quarters — with local cafes and a residential feel; good for a quieter, characterful stay near the centre.

A modern, car-light passivhaus district built on former rail land west of the station, with new-build apartments, wide green promenades, cinemas and family amenities; the most contemporary and affordable area, handy for the Hauptbahnhof but a tram ride from the old town.
lodging: House of Hütter – Heidelberg Suites & Spa

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe to drink everywhere.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 5am to around 1am; a Moonliner night-bus network covers weekend nights.
transit.pay: No tap-in gates: buy tickets in the RNV/VRN app, at machines, or from the driver, and validate before boarding; one ticket covers RNV trams and buses across the VRN network. A single ride in Heidelberg is about €3 (~$3.20) and a day ticket about €7.50. Staying weeks? The €58/month Deutschland-Ticket covers local transit nationwide. The Bergbahn funicular up to the castle and Königstuhl is priced separately.

transit.m: Lufthansa Express Bus direct from FRA to Heidelberg (~1 hr)
Train via Mannheim to Heidelberg Hbf (~1 hr)

tip.r: Service is included by law; locals round the bill up to the next euro or add about 5-10% for good service, handed to the server rather than left on the table.
